html:
SMTO-CAP-0011 — SMTO tried to use a tool before it was ready for this Task

GUID: a4f71a80-9982-4df6-a6c6-d81f03cecc0b
Slug: tool-discovery-required
Domain: CAP · Subsystem: cap

What happened

  • SMTO's Agent tried to use a tool before loading its instructions for this Task, or the tool stopped being available. Nothing was run, and the Agent usually loads the tool and tries again.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Watch the Task. If it loads the tool by itself and then uses it, you don't need to do anything. SMTO makes the Agent load a tool's current instructions before using it, and the Agent does this by itself.
  2. If the Task stops, open Capabilities by the message box and find the tool. If it shows Unavailable, fix the reason shown, for example with the Skill's Configure button. A tool that needs setup or a sign-in can't be used until that is done.
  3. If the tool works on another computer, open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for that Gateway. A Gateway that went offline makes its tools unavailable partway through a Task.
  4. Once the tool is available, ask SMTO to continue the Task. The Agent can then load the tool and carry on from where it stopped.

What success looks like

  • The Task loads the tool, uses it, and moves on without this message.

If it still fails

  • Send Copy error details to the person who manages SMTO; they show which tool wasn't ready. Don't switch a tool away from Never just to get past this unless you really want SMTO to use it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • ToolCatalog.validate_name rejected the call because the registered tool was not advertised for the current decision (discovery_required) or is no longer available in this run's catalog (stale_or_not_advertised_in_current_catalog); nothing executed.

What this means

  • The registered tool has not been advertised for this decision under the discovery guard, even if an implementation exists. Capability discovery and registration describe what this run may request. They do not grant operating-system permission, override exclusions or authorize execution by themselves.

Why this can happen

  • The registered tool has not been advertised for this decision under the discovery guard, even if an implementation exists.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the current advertised set with the requested exact name; use discovery while retaining exclusions.

How to fix it

  • Have the Agent call discover_tools for the tool's Skill or exact capability_id so the declaration is advertised, then rebuild the arguments from that declaration (validate_name and _discover in src/agent_runtime/native/catalog.py). If tool_availability reports the tool unavailable, fix the reported prerequisite (configuration, credentials, platform or Gateway connectivity); discovery never overrides exclusions.
  • Use discover_tools to obtain the supported tool declaration in this run, then construct the exact arguments. Discovery does not override exclusions.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Discovery advertises the allowed tool before a call is constructed and admitted.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Capability discovery and registration describe what this run may request. They do not grant operating-system permission, override exclusions or authorize execution by themselves.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
